claims.statement: Fork-workflow approval selection evaluates both PR author and triggering-event actor; a required approval is performed by a repository writer.

First-time approval policies can be bypassed after an innocuous merged contribution, even within someone else's PR. New-platform-user policy requires both new account status and no previous merged contribution; first-time policy only requires the latter. All-external policy covers users outside repository membership/ownership and organization membership.
The UI procedure ends with saving the selected setting; describing this step is not evidence it was applied.

Repository writers may review approval-required contributor PR workflows using PR navigation, changed-file inspection and the approval panel. Included navigation and inspection fragments are dependencies, not implied independent certification; approval is permission to execute, not evidence of safe execution.

The setting offers broad read/write token defaults or restricted contents/packages read defaults. Its 'all permissions' wording needs permission-specific reconciliation, including read-only or non-readable permission types; this UI choice is not an actual grant.

Before approving PR-branch workflow execution, inspect all proposed changes with special attention to workflow-file changes. Unchanged workflow files alone do not establish that branch code or dependencies are safe.
In this matrix fragment's context, variable-name comparisons are case-insensitive, so OS and os identify the same variable; this is not a universal statement about every configuration key.

The pinned source announces a public-repository pull_request_target blocking default with a stated enforcement date of November 2, 2026. This dated announcement is not present effective-enforcement evidence or a universal private-repository rule; live behavior and linked exceptions require separate verification.
Push branch and tag filters can include or exclude names; each inclusion key is mutually exclusive with its corresponding ignore key for the same event.
Defining only a branch or tag filter excludes events for the undefined ref type; defining neither admits both types. Branch and path filters jointly require both predicates.
Ref filters use glob rather than arbitrary regex syntax; special characters in literal ref names must be escaped. The linked pattern reference is separate evidence.

Push inclusion examples match branch names main, mona/octocat and releases/**, and tags v2 or v1.* against ref names in their respective namespaces. Example ref names are illustrative, not required target branches or observed runs.

Ignore-filter examples suppress pushes for mona/octocat, releases/**-alpha branches and v2 or v1.* tags. The prose mentions branches/tags while demonstrating ignore keys; this must be interpreted with actual exclusion semantics rather than conflating include and ignore filters.
Mixed inclusion/exclusion uses the include key with negative patterns, not both include and ignore keys; a negative pattern requires at least one positive pattern for that ref type.
Filter order is significant: a later matching negative excludes a previously included ref, while a later matching positive re-includes it.

The example includes releases/** then excludes releases/**-alpha, admitting stable examples and excluding alpha suffix examples. This is an illustrative filter, not required release naming policy or executed verification.
